title: Tracking — Golden Signals
description: Delivery state and error rate for the Tracking service. NOTE ON WHY THIS IS NOT SHAPED LIKE THE USERS/ORDERS DASHBOARDS: Tracking emits no per-request log line — it has no 'request completed' log, so http_route and duration_ms are absent from its records and the usual request-rate/latency/top-routes panels would all be empty. It is instead built on the CloudWatch metrics it does publish (hence PromQL, not SQL), plus its SQLAlchemy statement stream. Adding a request log to the service would make the log-based panels possible; see the note on the last panel.

panels.title: Orders — finished vs in progress
panels.description: DELIVERED is the state machine's terminal status, so 'finished' is the domain's own invariant. One tracking per order (uq_tracking_order_id), so these counts are order counts. A gauge, hence max() — sum() would add every sample in the window and report a multiple of the truth.

panels.title: Orders with a tracking record
panels.description: DELIVERED + IN_PROGRESS — every order Tracking knows about. Compare against orders_total on the Business Metrics dashboard: the difference is orders whose init-tracking call failed, a failure mode Orders accepts deliberately rather than failing the order. Normally zero.

panels.title: HTTP errors by class
panels.description: 4xx/5xx only. The 5xx series is captured through an explicit exception branch in the ASGI middleware: Starlette's ServerErrorMiddleware sits outside every add_middleware layer, so an unhandled exception's 500 never reaches a send wrapper and would otherwise go uncounted (see docs/lessons/2026-08-12-server-error-middleware-outside-pure-asgi-middleware.md).

panels.title: Log volume
panels.description: Records per interval from the tracking container. Mostly SQLAlchemy statement echo today — including the metrics gauge's own COUNT every 15s — because the service emits no per-request log. Useful as a liveness signal: a flat line means the service stopped logging.

queries.query: SELECT histogram(_timestamp) AS x_axis_1, COUNT(*) AS y_axis_1 FROM logs WHERE service_name = 'tracking' GROUP BY x_axis_1

panels.title: Recent warnings and errors
panels.description: Severity-based rather than status-based, because Tracking logs no HTTP status. KNOWN GAP: this service has no per-request log line, so a failing request only appears here if it also logged an error. Adding a 'request completed' log (as Users and Orders have) would let this dashboard carry the same request-rate, latency and top-routes panels they do.

queries.query: SELECT _timestamp, severity_text, message FROM logs WHERE service_name = 'tracking' AND severity_text IN ('WARN', 'ERROR', 'FATAL') ORDER BY _timestamp DESC
